recipes.name: Stewed Tomatoes (Gobbledygook)
ingredients_raw: 1 (28 ounce) can whole peeled tomatoes, with liquid
3 slices stale bread, torn into pieces

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 1 1/2 quart baking dish.
Stir the tomatoes, bread, sugar, butter, salt, and pepper in a bowl; pour into the prepared dish.
Bake until hot and the tomatoes are tender, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Stewed Tomatoes (Gobbledygook)
raw_recipe.description: Canned tomatoes are baked with stale bread, butter, and sugar in this southern-style side dish.

review.reviewBody: tryed recipe yesterday,my wife is a southern girl and raised on stewed tomatoes. followed recipe word for word, she said these are the best. please try it you won't be sorry, and thanks for the recipe.says bacondebaker

I wanted to see if stewed tomatoes are still as discusting as when my mother would force me to eat them as a child. To my surprise, I enjoyed this dish! my mother always used white bread, but I only had 12 grain bread on hand. I halved this recipe, and used only 1 tablespoon sugar. I really liked the 12 grain bread in this, I think I will always use it to make it a tad healthier. Thanks for sharing your recipe!

Made this yesterday with some stale french bread needing to be used. It was absolutely delicious. I cut the recipe in half and ate the whole dish. Only change was to saute some onions in the butter and add to the dish. (I eat onions in everything!). Thanks for the recipe.

These stewed tomatoes were better than the kind my Mom used to make, sorry Mom!!
The only thing that I did different was lightly toast the bread. And maybe next time I may add some sauteed onions.
Can't wait to make these again!!
Amazing! I added a small dash of ground gloves, I had sourdough/rosemary bread and added a half cup of broth. Heaven!

I'm another woman who STILL cannot control the child within. I always thought this dish was a punishment for something I'd done. My mother finally gave up saying she could'nt stand the awful faces I made (they ruined the dish for her and she'd eat anything!) Fast forward 6 decades - Holey moley batman! These taste really good!! Although Mum always put sugar on tomato-anything ( it's a fruit afterall ) I'm pretty sure that she would be perfectly happy with 1/3 C of sugar. in this recipe. Thank you X3!! P.S. I'm pretty sure she's above us all with a satisfied grin on her face.

Oh Man!!! I couldn't even remember what this was called, but wanted it today, so began to search, and here it is. For dietary reasons, I cut the sugar way back, left out the butter and salt, and boiled 6 fresh plum tomatoes in a little water, toasted the bread a bit and then served it with bow-tie pasta for dinner. But it was the texture, the flavor, the side dish I wanted. I know many say that means I didn't make the recipe, therefore shouldn't evaluate it. Sorry, but I use this site for inspiration more than imitation. And this inspired me. Thank you for posting it.

I grew up in the Midwest and my mother made "breaded" tomatoes in the summer when we had a bounty of tomatoes. She did not add sugar to the pot, but instead put the sugar bowl on the table and let each person sweeten the tomatoes to his or her own taste. This recipe brought back wonderful memories.
Ok, I didn't have whole tomatoes so I tried it with crushed tomatoes and added a little water to thin it out. It's the bomb and I can't wait to try it again with the correct tomatoes.

Yes I tried it and I liked it! I had not heard of baking stewed tomatoes. I substituted fresh garden tomatoes in season for the canned tomatoes and turned out good. You might add a little water when using the fresh tomatoes.

Tomatoes from the garden blanched and skinned. Diced onions and celery, toasted bread,salt and pepper. Sugar definitely optional. Cook on stovetop.Yum! Have to admit i will eat any stewed tomatoes cooked any way, but I prefer my version.
I followed your directions and we loved it. It's budget friendly and and filling. I even made it a second time with store bought salad croutons, on top of the stove, and that was pretty good too.
Use fresh tomatoes! It's wonderful!!! Wouldn't change a thing with the recipe.

This is the exact recipe my grandmother made except about half the sugar she called it stewed tomatoes, it was still sweet and delicious. When i tasted what ofher people called stewed tomatoes - i was kind of disappointed

My mother made this often when I was a little guy. (I'm 86 years old now} We all loved it. She called it tomato cush. My older brother phoned me recently to get the recipe and really got upset when I told him for each ingredient "use however much tastes good to you".
I have made this for years I used stewed can tomatoes buttered toast torn to pieces salt and pepper on top of the stove. Sugar sometimes.
My Mama made this all the time, but she called it Tomato Pudding! Yummy goodness!
....and I thought my mother was making this because she couldn't find anything else to feed the family when I was young!!! It's one of my absolute favorites!
Reminds me of my childhood in the Deep South! Yum!
I made some on New Ywars Day. Everyone said it was the best stewed tomato ever. Great everyone enjoyed them and ask for the recipe.
